verdicts.rationale: The scroll earns its place. MEASURED at 373x410: key-empty shows 3 rows of an open list running from y 301 to 529, and after the proposed scroll of 118.7 px it shows 7 rows (182 to 410) with the field label at 133, under the 89 px pinned header. The dial's rotation search goes from 0 visible rows to 8 after 175 px, label at 199 under the 105 px header. Zero writes. The band scrolls away (6 px and 0 px left visible), which has a precedent: after 'Pick another reading' the status block already sits entirely under the header (y -63 to 53).
verdicts.regression_risk: The page moves when a list opens. A smooth scroll would add an animation system. Scrolling back on close would double the motion. At zoom widths the header can be unpinned (data-pin-off), so a cap based on the header's bottom would scroll the label off-screen.
verdicts.revised_correction: Scroll only on an open the person starts (a click, the first typed character, or Down Arrow), never on an echo, rebuild or refresh, and only when the list's bottom is past the viewport. Scroll instantly by min(overflow, labelTop - pinnedHeaderHeight - 8), where pinnedHeaderHeight is 0 when the header is not pinned. Never scroll back on close. For picker targets, reveal() aligns the field's label under the header instead of centering it (X11).
verdicts.acceptance_test: 373x410: clicking #picker-search on key-empty leaves at least 6 fully visible rows with #picker-label fully below the pinned header; the dial-configured rotation search leaves at least 4; closing the list leaves scrollY unchanged; zero writes. 320x560 key-empty, where the list already fits: scrollY changes by 0. 189x410: the label stays inside the viewport.
verdicts.evidence: MEASURED power\power.json r17 (before, opened and after for both fixtures) and x11 (status y -63 to 53, header bottom 89); r17-key-empty-open.png, r17-key-empty-scrolled.png, r17-dial-configured-rotation-*.png, x11-pick-another.png.

verdicts.rationale: Agree with keeping the moved chip in view and with Alt+Home and Alt+End, but only for keyboard moves; reject the sticky toolbar. P04 measured a chip-to-toolbar gap of up to 422 px on a 410 px panel, so after a toolbar click the moved chip and the pressed button cannot both stay in view. A sticky toolbar would add 34 px of pinned chrome (28 px plus margins) to the dial's measured 105 px header: 139 px, or 34% of 410. That is past the one-third limit the header itself is held to, and it covers the bottom chip row. Scrolling on Alt+Arrow matches what arrow selection already does, and Alt+Home and Alt+End extend the existing Home and End selection.
verdicts.regression_risk: If toolbar presses auto-scroll, the pressed button moves out from under the pointer and focus can scroll off-screen. Alt+Home is unverified in QtWebEngine.
verdicts.revised_correction: After Alt+Arrow, Alt+Home or Alt+End (focus in the listbox), scroll the moved chip into view with block 'nearest', as arrow selection already does. After a toolbar activation, by pointer or by Enter, never scroll: the pressed button stays put. No position: sticky toolbar. Add Alt+Home and Alt+End to R52's real-host owner check.
verdicts.acceptance_test: A 37-member flat rotation at 373x410: 36 Alt+Left presses leave the moved chip inside the viewport after each; 36 Earlier clicks leave the Earlier button's viewport rect unchanged (within 0.5 px) after each; Alt+Home moves member 37 to place 1 with one press and one write; no element inside #rotation-box has position: sticky.
verdicts.evidence: READ power.json P04 (p2-373.json, maximum chip-to-toolbar gap 422 px). MEASURED power\power.json r23.headH 105px. READ pi.css .hw-set-tools margin 2px 0 4px, pi.css:103-108 (the one-third rule), pi-common.js:556 (selection scrolls into view), pi-common.js:4146 (Home and End select).

verdicts.rationale: Parity is good: both checklists come from one factory, and the detail checklist shows '+ all' (7 buttons) while the rotation checklist shows none. The control is visually quiet: 36.2x24 px, 11 px link blue, #7c7c7c border. The problem is reversal. One press can add dozens of members (for example a whole Motherboard source), which grows the rotation list, the overview and the Reading colors list, and the rotation has no bulk removal.
verdicts.regression_risk: MEASURED: with '+ all' each source header is 32 px tall instead of 24.8 px, and at 320 two of seven source names are cut (none without it). Source names are what tell identical readings apart (R07). A bulk add without a bulk undo means many single removals. The list's 158 px scroller shows fewer rows.
verdicts.revised_correction: Use the detail checklist's component and style unchanged. The aria-label names the target group, for example 'Add every reading of CPU to group GPU'. Ship only together with a one-press reversal: R25's Undo in the set note ('Added 10 from CPU. Undo'). Optionally draw '+ all' in both checklists with the .hw-link hit-area idiom so the headers stay 24.8 px.
verdicts.acceptance_test: dial-configured at 373x410: the rotation checklist shows 7 '+ all' buttons whose computed style equals the detail checklist's; one press on CPU adds its non-member readings in tree order to the collector group, with exactly one write per field; Undo restores rotationKeys and rotationGroups byte-identical with one write; the list keeps its scroll.
verdicts.evidence: MEASURED power\power.json r22_detail and r22_rotation (addAllCount 7 vs 0); addall\addall.json (header rowH 32 vs 24.8; nameCut true for CPU and Motherboard at 320); r22-320.png. READ pi-common.js:2350-2362 (factory), 1718-1733 (detail add-all is add-only).

verdicts.rationale: The toolbar follows the selection into that group's reserved slot. MEASURED: selecting in group 2 after group 1 moves the Later button from y 151.3 to 265.3, a 114 px jump, and the old Later point then holds group 1's inert hint. A cross-group move from the toolbar therefore relocates the pressed control, and a second click lands on the hint: harmless, but the flow breaks. MEASURED: the grouped toolbar has 1.2 px spare at 320, so a separate 'move to group' control would wrap the slot. The edge-crossing semantics are coherent, because the chip continues in the same direction across the boundary.
verdicts.regression_risk: The Earlier and Later buttons lose their 'you are at the edge' disabled cue. An overshoot moves a reading into the neighbor group. Scroll compensation cannot work at the page bottom. E2e checks that assume disabled edges need updating.
verdicts.revised_correction: Accept edge crossing: Later at the end of group N moves the reading to the start of N+1, and Earlier at the start of N moves it to the end of N-1. After a cross-group move from the toolbar, scroll by the toolbar's displacement so the pressed button keeps its viewport position; where the page cannot scroll that far, scroll as far as possible and keep focus on the button. Alt+Arrow keeps focus in the new group's listbox and scrolls the chip into view. Announce 'moved to group GPU, 1 of 3'. At an edge the aria-label and title say 'Move X to group GPU'. Visible labels stay the same and no control is added.
verdicts.acceptance_test: dial-groups at 373x410: select CPU CCD1 (last in group 1) and click Later: it is first in group 2, with one write per field; the Later button's viewport rect is equal (within 1 px) before and after; the chip is in the viewport. Click Earlier at the same point: rotationGroups is byte-identical to the start. Later on the last member of the last group stays aria-disabled.
verdicts.evidence: MEASURED power\power.json r23 (laterG1 y 151.3, laterG2 y 265.3, toolbarJumpY 114, elementAtOldLaterPoint 'hw-set-tools-hint'); r23-sheet.png; tools\tools.json dial-groups@320 spareRight 1.2. READ pi-common.js:527-540 (placeRotationTools), pi.css:1379-1383 (slot).

band_prototype.preferred: P1's wording, built as 'P1b': one line reading 'Theme  Default (shared: Void)  Change' or 'Theme  Ember (this key only)' ('this dial only' on the dial). Change is a flex:none sibling after the ellipsizing #theme-current span, not inside it, so it keeps the .hw-link 24 px hit area. There is no help line except on an unconfigured key and for an unknown stored value. At zoom widths (below 240 px) the parenthetical and Change render under the chips, where the help line sits today. MEASURED answer to the 320 question: P1 does not wrap at 320, or even at 305, because .hw-look-current is white-space: nowrap (pi.css:376-382); the longest line, 'Default (shared: Ultraviolet) Change', fits uncut. The band stays 106.1 px for Default, Ember, explicit Ultraviolet and Default-on-Ultraviolet, on key and dial, at 373, 320 and 305, so a pick does not change the height. That is 19 px shorter than P0, and it brings the Display section's first label onto the first screen at 373.
band_prototype.conditions: 1. Change never sits inside the overflow:hidden span. P1 as prototyped measured 17 to 18 px of hit height at 373 and 320 (P1b: 24 to 25; P0: 23 to 24), below the 24 px floor of contract 3, and only 0 to 7.7 of 45.3 px of Change is visible at 189 and 160. 2. The dial says '(this dial only)'; band-proto.mjs:25 hard-codes 'this key only'. 3. R04 (the line reports only the stored and drawn theme) lands first or together; otherwise hovering Paper renders 'Paper (this key only)', claiming a stored choice that does not exist. 4. Below 240 px, keep the scope text and Change under the chips. P1b there cuts the resolved theme ('Defaul... Change' at 160, '(sha...' at 189; lineCut true), which breaks contract 1 where P0 still shows 'Default · Void'. Wrapping the line above the chips (my P1w) makes the chip row move 16 to 33 px under the pointer on a pick (160 px: 231.5 vs 198.6; 189 px: 214.7 vs 198.6). P0 stays at 217.3 across picks at both zoom widths. 5. Keep the help line only for an unconfigured key and an unknown stored value. On an unconfigured key this means 125.2 px until the first pick, then a one-time 19 px upward shift of everything under the band; the chips never move. The unknown state stays at 141.3 px, the same as P0; trim its line to '"neon" (unknown)' so 'draws Void' is not said twice. 6. Point the radiogroup's aria-describedby at the scope text, because P1 hides #theme-help, which it references today. 7. Update the e2e help-text assertion (e2e-pi-panels.mjs:437) and the y baselines. Acceptance: at 373x410, 320x560 and 305x560, on key and dial, all eight picks give a band height of 106 px (within 0.5), #theme-current is not cut, Change is fully visible with a hit height of at least 24 px, and hovering or focusing chips leaves the line unchanged with zero writes. At 189x410 and 160x410, all eight picks give equal chip-row tops (within 0.5 px), the full resolved theme name is visible without a tooltip, and Change is fully visible.
band_prototype.rejected_because: P0: 'Default' appears three times, it adds a third way of saying 'inherited' next to the Text color select's '(shared: X)' idiom, and it is 19 px taller at no gain. P2: 125.2 px everywhere, identical to P0; it trims one 'Default' but keeps the '·' idiom and saves nothing. P3: the band height changes on a pick at every width (124.2 vs 140.3 at 373, 320 and 305; 216.3 vs 232.4 at 160), breaking the code's own rule 'a pick never moves what is below' (pi-common.js:3506-3507), and it leaves 'Theme' as a bare label over the chips. P1 exactly as prototyped: the Change target is clipped to 17 to 18 px and disappears at zoom. P1b or P1w without the zoom rule: at zoom either the resolved theme is ellipsized away or the chips move under the pointer on a pick.

new_concerns: The grouped rotation toolbar has 1.2 px spare at 320 (MEASURED tools\tools.json). Any added toolbar control, whether X06's caption, an Undo button or a move-to-group select, wraps the slot from 34 to 66 px and breaks the guarantee that selecting moves nothing. Fixes for R23, R24 and R25 must not add anything to the toolbar row.

Two idioms for destructive actions: R02 (batch 1) uses arm-then-confirm for group removal, while R25 would use Undo for member removal. If the set-note Undo is built, consider it for group removal too: one idiom, no extra press. I am flagging this, not overriding batch 1.

Lab artifact relevant to R44: the simulator's theme store keeps the previous fixture's shared theme when a fixture has empty globals. key-empty rendered 'Default · Ultraviolet' after a run with shared Ultraviolet (MEASURED band\band.json), so fixture measurements can depend on run order. Force explicit globals, or reset the store in setFixture.

'+ all' makes each source header 32 px tall instead of 24.8 px, and at 320 it cuts 2 of 7 source names (MEASURED addall\addall.json). The source name is what tells identical readings apart (R07). If R22 ships, consider the .hw-link hit-area idiom in both checklists.

The 'Change' link in P1 moves a shared-scope action to the top line of the per-key band, where it becomes the most saturated text above the chips. This is a low-confidence walkthrough risk: keep '(shared: X)' immediately before it and keep the accessible name 'Change the shared theme'.

X11's stated trade-off (the status block scrolls out of view while picking) already happens today: after 'Pick another reading' the status block sits entirely under the 89 px pinned header (y -63 to 53, MEASURED power\power.json x11). So the explanation of why the reading is missing is off-screen while the person picks its replacement; consider repeating its one-line cause in the picker's label or help.
